messages:
maria: FYI compliance just sent a hit about traces containing emails/phones coming from router-service. They attached sample spans that include `http.request.headers.x-user-email` in attributes. We need a short proposal before EOD.

ken: Oof. Is this coming from request headers we preserve right now? I thought we had an attributes filter.

maria: Looks like we weren't filtering `http.request.headers.*` across all services. One service added it for debugging and collector allowed it through.

sasha: Quick Q — do we want to redact at the app, collector, or exporter? Each has tradeoffs (latency, trace completeness, audit).

pm-robin: From product/regulatory view: minimal surface exposed to third-party exporters. Prefer collector-side enforced defaults + policy that apps must opt-in via annotation for any raw PII.

sec-jen: Strong vote for collector-level hygiene. Also need audit trail: who un-redacted/queried raw values and why. That probably means storing raw PII only in an encrypted audit vault with strict IAM and recording access.

ken: Implementation idea: At collector, run attributes processor to scrub known keys and pseudonymize values with HMAC-SHA256 using a rotating key in KMS. Keep the pseudonym in spans for debugging and joinability, but raw goes to secure store.

maria: Example attributes processor snippet I'm thinking of:
```yaml
processors:
  attributes/redact:
    actions:
      - key: "http.request.headers.x-user-email"
        action: delete
      - key: "user.email"
        action: hash
    hash:
      algorithm: "hmac_sha256"
      key_ref: "kms://projects/redwood/keys/trace-hmac"
```

sasha: Nice. Two follow-ups: 1) hash vs encrypt (hash is irreversible, better for privacy but you lose ability to recover). 2) exporters: block raw attribute exports to any external backend by default; only allow hashed/pseudonymized attributes.

sec-jen: For compliance audits we sometimes must show original values to data-protection officers. If we hash irreversibly, we need a separate workflow: store raw in an encrypted blob store (sealed with an HSM) and return only with authorized unwrap + full audit. That matches legal requirements.

pm-robin: Operationally that means: collector redacts or hashes for normal pipelines; if an app opts into full store, collector clones the span to a secure pipeline that encrypts and pushes to the vault. Access to that pipeline must be gated by an approval workflow.

ken: Also need to think about retention. Default traces retention is 30d; secure vault retention for raw PII should be much shorter (e.g., 90 days) and supported by an automated purge + retention logs.

maria: Agree. Suggest default telemetry retention stays but a flag `telemetry.pi_iraw_retention_days` controls secure vault TTL. Also add a slow canary: enable collector filter in staging for 48h to validate no high-cardinality explosion in pseudonyms.

sasha: One more angle: OTLP exporters and third-party integrations. We must enforce exporter-level denylist for attributes, or an exporter wrapper that re-checks attributes before sending. We can't rely on every exporter respecting our collector filters.

ken: We can implement an exporter wrapper plugin that rejects spans containing blacklisted attribute patterns and logs an event to the audit stream. That makes exports fail-fast and visible.

observability-bot: deploy-notice: collector config change `attributes/redact` scheduled for canary cluster on 2026-04-02 10:00 UTC. CI job `otel-collector-config-check` will run.

sec-jen: Also need to add an audit schema: who requested raw access, who approved, access justification, timestamp, and HSM unwrap key id. That record must be immutable and retained per compliance (suggest 7 years).

pm-robin: OK — deliverables: 1) collector attributes policy (redact/hash + secure clone) PR, 2) exporter wrapper that enforces denylist, 3) secure vault + audit workflow doc, 4) retention/purge automation. Can we get owners?

maria: I'll take 1 and coordinate canary.

ken: I'll prototype the exporter wrapper and add unit tests.

sec-jen: I'll draft the audit schema and vault access policy with legal.

sasha: I'll add test cases to the eval harness to ensure attributes are stripped for external exporters and create a post-deploy checklist.

pm-robin: Thanks — please post PR links here when ready. Also ping me for any policy decisions that require product sign-off. :thumbsup:

maria: Will do. If anyone spots other attribute names (phone, ssn, credit_card), add to the denylist in the PR.

ken: Noted — I'll add a wildcard rule for `http.request.headers.*` but keep a safe allowlist for `user-agent` etc.

observability-bot: ci/build:otel-collector-config-check succeeded for branch `maria/redact-pii` (3 changed files).

maria: CI passed. I'll open the canary rollout ticket and set the 48h window.

pm-robin: Great progress. We'll review after canary and then schedule org-wide rollout.
